example_input: @dsh-superagent please fix the failing parser test on main
note: A maintainer's comment on a watched issue traced through the GitHub Source, Intake, an admission Eval, the Mandate and Ticket it creates, the worker Session that does the work, and the result that returns to the same conversation.

modules.label: github-trigger.ts:55 - Trigger translation: stable ids, human, addressed
github.ts:274 - the polling round, in order

steps.narrative: The GitHub Source's poll round (notifications, repository streams, open-Ticket PRs, subscribed Threads) picks up the maintainer's comment. Translation gives it a stable Trigger id, a primary Thread (the issue), human: true from the account type, and addressed: true because the text mentions the agent's login. Nothing has been decided yet - the Trigger is just an honest record of what happened.
steps.title: The comment becomes a Trigger

modules.label: intake.ts:16 - Intake.receive: dedup, scope, fan-out, Eval queuing
engine.ts:40 - Engine.receive

steps.narrative: Engine.receive hands the Trigger to Intake, which stores it exactly once (a redelivery is answered 'duplicate'), records it on its Threads and their correlations, and fans it out to Tickets subscribed to those Threads - none yet for a new issue. Because no worker owns this follow-up, the Trigger is queued for Eval on its primary Thread.
steps.representation:
receive(trigger)
  -> stored (dedup by Trigger id)
  -> fan-out to subscribed Tickets: []
  -> queue for Eval on Thread(issue 412)
steps.title: Intake stores it once and fans it out

modules.label: passes.ts:22 - the 2 s serialized pump
engine.ts:65 - Engine.evaluateDue

steps.narrative: Passes run every two seconds and on demand, serialized so at most one runs at a time: due effects first, then Engine.evaluateDue. It expires or requeues stale Evals, resumes paused Tickets the current Policy admits, and starts an Eval for the issue's Thread, batching its waiting Triggers.
steps.representation:
every 2 s (and on request):
  effects.kick()
  engine.evaluateDue()
    -> start Eval for Thread(issue 412)
steps.title: A pass finds the Thread due

modules.label: evals.ts:71 - Evals.start: batching, gate, assessor.request
assessment.ts:85 - MasterAssessor delivery via the assessment effect
policy.ts:167 - settingsPolicy().gate, in precedence order

steps.narrative: Evals.start classifies the Trigger through the Policy gate: a listed person addressing the agent is the strongest class and is judged on its own. The candidate card is delivered to the main Session through a durable effect - delivery starts the Eval's deadline (default 120 s) - and the MasterAssessor judges it from the Trigger's stored text. It fetches nothing: the record it sees is the record that was stored.
steps.representation:
gate(trigger) = addressed (listed, human)
assessor.request(candidate)
  deadline starts on delivery: 120 s
  judgement: accept | stop | ignore
steps.title: The gate classifies, the assessor judges

modules.label: tickets.ts:29 - Tickets.create, one transaction
model.ts:96 - Mandate and MandateBasis
outbox.ts:18 - receipt first, then the reply effect

steps.narrative: The assessor's accept becomes Engine.decide, and Tickets.create writes everything in one transaction: the Ticket, its Mandate (basis: addressed, stamped with the Policy revision), its Subscriptions, and its first Assignment. The acknowledgement is queued through the Outbox - receipt persisted first - and the Executor is told to start. All of it commits, or none of it does.
steps.representation:
one transaction:
  Ticket + Mandate{via: addressed}
  + Subscriptions + Assignment#1
  + outbox.acknowledge()
  + executor.start(ticket)
steps.title: Accept mints the Mandate and the Ticket, atomically

modules.label: dsh.ts:1 - DshExecutor: one Session and directory per Ticket
dsh.ts:240 - the prepare command and PrepareFailed
sessions.ts:137 - Sessions.ensure sets danger-full-access

steps.narrative: DshExecutor creates Session worker-<ticketId> and a fresh directory for the Ticket, running the team's prepare command first (10-minute cap; a failed prepare is recorded, not retried). Sessions.ensure sets the preset the code names danger-full-access: the worker runs as the operator's OS user, without an approval step. A Ticket directory and Session are reused across the Ticket's Assignments.
steps.representation:
session: worker-<ticketId>
  dir: <stateDir>/work/<ticket name>
  prepare command (<= 10 min)
  preset: danger-full-access
steps.title: A worker Session starts in the Ticket's own directory

modules.label: cordis.patch.yml:35 - worker preset: 5 s shell backgrounding
background.ts:1 - shell jobs and subagents keep the worker busy
executor.ts:75 - orchestrator_report: claim the PR, record the report

steps.narrative: Inside its dsh Session - the borrowed turn loop from teardown #15 - the worker investigates and edits. The worker preset moves a foreground shell command to a background job after 5 seconds, so the Session can take the next message instead of blocking on a test run. When a turn ends with jobs still running, the Ticket keeps its worker slot; background work gets at most 30 minutes per turn. Progress reports stay on the Ticket - they do not become messages to the maintainer.
steps.representation:
worker turn (dsh loop):
  shell > 5 s -> background job
  turn ends, jobs running -> slot kept
  background limit: 30 min per turn
  report(progress) -> stays on the Ticket
steps.title: Work runs; long shells move to the background

modules.label: assignments.ts:95 - Assignments.report and followsDone
github-pull.ts:30 - a PR binds to a Ticket by origin or branch
replies.ts:18 - the four gated reply kinds

steps.narrative: The worker opens its pull request - bound to the Ticket because it is agent-authored on the Ticket's branch - and reports ready. The Ticket does not end on the report alone: it ends when the Threads it follows are done, so the PR merging (or closing) is what closes the Ticket, as merged or closed. The result reply goes through the Outbox to the original issue conversation, the only kind of channel write the core can make, gated by its own rule.
steps.representation:
report(ready, pr claimed)
  Ticket ends when followsDone:
    every opened Thread closed
  -> outcome: merged | closed
  outbox: result -> issue 412
steps.title: Ready is a claim; the merged PR is the proof

title: One request, end to end: an issue comment becomes a pull request
